nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light powers the pine forest, the dune grasses and the algae of the shallow lagoon.

nodes.name: Drifting sand and dunes
nodes.desc: The spit is a long sand ridge with some of Europe's highest moving dunes. Sand shapes which plants can grow and where forest can take hold.

nodes.name: River nutrients
nodes.desc: The Neman River supplies most of the water entering the shallow Curonian Lagoon, bringing the nutrients that feed its algae.

nodes.name: Soil fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down pine litter, reeds, algae and carcasses, returning nutrients to the thin sandy soil and the lagoon.

nodes.name: Scots pine
nodes.desc: The main forest tree of the spit, much of it planted since the 1800s to hold moving sand in place. Its shoots and seeds feed deer, moose and rodents.

nodes.name: European marram grass
nodes.desc: A tough dune grass whose roots bind loose sand on the beach and foredunes.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: Forms reed beds along the lagoon shore, giving food and cover to waterbirds, beavers and fish.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting algae in the shallow lagoon. Nutrient-rich water has led to confirmed algal blooms there.

nodes.name: Striped field mouse
nodes.desc: A small rodent of fields and forest edges that eats seeds and plant material. It is prey for stoats, gulls and wolves.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: An omnivore that roots for plant matter and small animals in the forest. Wolves prey on it.

nodes.name: European roe deer
nodes.desc: A small browser of the forest edge, feeding on shoots, leaves and berries. The best-recorded deer near the spit.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: The largest browser in the area, feeding on twigs and shoots of trees and shrubs. Wolves and white-tailed eagles feed on it, the eagles as carrion.

nodes.name: Eurasian beaver
nodes.desc: Feeds on bark, shoots and water plants, and builds dams and lodges along waterways.

nodes.name: Mute swan
nodes.desc: A large waterbird that grazes on aquatic plants in the lagoon and its reed beds.

nodes.name: Roach
nodes.desc: A common freshwater fish that eats plankton, plants and small invertebrates. Perch, cormorants and eagles eat it.

nodes.name: Stoat
nodes.desc: A small hunter of mice, voles and small birds in dunes and forest edges.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: An omnivorous scavenger that feeds on carcasses and small animals.

nodes.name: Herring gull
nodes.desc: An opportunistic feeder on the coast, taking fish, small animals and scraps.

nodes.name: Great cormorant
nodes.desc: A diving fish-eater that is abundant on the lagoon and coast.

nodes.name: European perch
nodes.desc: A predatory fish of the lagoon that eats smaller fish and invertebrates.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Hunts deer, moose and wild boar in the forests.

nodes.name: White-tailed eagle
nodes.desc: Hunts fish and waterbirds around the lagoon and also scavenges carrion.
